explanation: Outer lanes are longer, which is why runners in the 200 m and 400 m start at staggered positions. Over a full lap, lane eight is more than 50 metres longer than lane one.

claims.text: One lap of the inside lane of a standard outdoor running track measures 400 metres.
A standard outdoor track lap is not 200, 500 or 800 metres.
In the 200 m and 400 m, runners start at staggered positions because outer lanes are longer.
With lanes about 1.22 m wide, a lap of lane eight is more than 50 metres longer than a lap of lane one.

evidence.restatement: A standard outdoor track measures 400 m along the inside lane (measured 30 cm out from the kerb).
The lap is not 200, 500 or 800 m.
The 200 m and 400 m use staggered starts because outer lanes have longer bends.
With 1.22 m lanes, lane eight's lap is about 2 x pi x 7 x 1.22 = 53.7 m longer than lane one's, or about 53 m allowing for the measuring lines (arithmetic re-run).
